messages:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Alert: spike detected — api-gateway-eu-west returning elevated 502/504s (5m window) — P99 latency up 3x. Auto-paged oncall.
olivia: i'm on it — oncall handover in 2m. grabbing dashboards.
sam: seeing a sharp jump from backend pool b (eu-west-1b) — 502 ratio ~12% on ingress for the last 3min.
jordan: confirmed, synthetic canary shows 502s on multiplexed requests. starting grep on proxy logs.
lee: @olivia FYI customers reporting chat timeouts. support-ops will surface top impacted orgs.
maya: adding trace IDs to the incident timeline: run: `grep "trace=" /var/log/proxy/* | head` and attach sample.
olivia: quick triage: 1) isolate whether this is routing vs upstream 2) check pool health 3) enable short-circuit fallback.
sam: tailing haproxy stats:

``` 
# echo "show stat" | socat unix-connect:/var/run/haproxy.sock stdio | grep -E "api-gw|FRONTEND"
"api-gw","BACKEND_B","...,srv_b1",…,scur=200,stot=45000,rate=120,hrsp_5xx=540
```
sam: backend_b srv_b1/2 showing increased hrsp_5xx counts.
jordan: grabbing k8s pod logs for svc-backend-b:
```
kubectl -n platform logs svc-backend-b-7f6c -c http | tail -n 50 | grep "504\|502"
```
jordan: seeing upstream socket timeout errors (ETIMEDOUT) and occasional 502 from proxy to upstream.
lee: traffic distribution note: traffic shifted to eu-west due to upstream regional failover at 17:02 UTC — could be related.
maya: support-ops: affected customers list? can you paste top 5 orgs + % of requests failing?
support-ops: top impacted orgs: AcmeCorp (18% of their requests), BrightAI (12%), NanoHealth (9%). We opened a support banner and emailed top SLA contacts.
olivia: immediate mitigations: 1) open a temporary circuit-breaker for backend_b 2) route new requests away from srv_b* 3) enable short TTL cache for common prefixes.
sam: applying iptables throttle? i'd rather flip routing weight to backend_a and decrease backend_b weight in the ingress balancer.
eng-runtime: agree with weight shift. preparing quick patch to routing table — will roll within 30s if tests pass.
olivia: can someone run a controlled failover to verify traffic shift doesn't increase latency elsewhere? small percent first.
eng-runtime: rolling traffic shift +10% every 30s, monitoring 5xx and p95.
sam: command used:
```
# curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/route-weight -d '{"service":"api-gw","weights":{"backend_a":0.85,"backend_b":0.15}}'
```
support-ops: bump: after initial shift 10%->backend_a, backend_b 5xx dropped to 3% within 90s, customer errors trending down.
jordan: collecting traces for a failing request. Found upstream connect timeout `connect: connection timed out` to srv_b2 at 17:04:12.
maya: creating timeline entry with sample trace ids: trace=abc123,trace=def456.
olivia: status update to execs: brief note ready — impacted customers identified, mitigation in progress (traffic shift + circuit-breaker), ETA 15m for stabilization.
lee: pending checks: DB connection pools on backend_b? Could be saturation. @sam can you query pool metrics.
sam: db pool usage for backend_b nodes shows connections ~98% on srv_b1 at 17:03:50.
eng-runtime: that explains timeouts — backend_b app threads exhausted then timed out proxy connections. we should keep traffic off until we fix pool.
olivia: plan: keep traffic shifted, restart svc-backend-b pods one-by-one with graceful drain, then bring weight back slowly. coordinate with infra.
eng-runtime: initiating rolling restart (graceful) for backend_b nodes now. command:
```
kubectl -n platform rollout restart deploy/svc-backend-b
```
jordan: restarting srv_b pods sequentially. monitoring error rate.
support-ops: customer comms updated: "We are investigating elevated gateway errors in EU; mitigation steps in progress. We'll follow up in 30 minutes." — sent to top impacted contacts.
lee: any downstream surge in backend_a after shifting weights? p95 increased slightly but within SLO.
maya: capturing metrics snapshot for postmortem: saved graphs for p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, open connections.
olivia: update: after two pods restarted, backend_b connection pool normalized and hrsp_5xx dropped to 0.8% — good signal.
sam: increasing backend_b weight back to 40% and observing.
eng-runtime: traffic moved back, monitoring shows stable 5xx <1% and latency norms restored.
support-ops: closing emergency banner for day users; will keep watch and send final customer note after incident review.
olivia: incident severity: Sev2 (partial customer impact, mitigation successful, no data loss). next steps: postmortem runbook, RCA focus on DB pool sizing + autoscaling thresholds + better circuit-breaker defaults.
maya: assigning postmortem owners: @jordan (logs/traces), @sam (pool sizing), @eng-runtime (autoscale + routing), @support-ops (customer comms).
olivia: nice job team — triage closed. if anything flares up, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
